title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-17
lineage: SBD > Reel Master (10 Inch Reels @ 15ips 1/2trk) > DAT > Sonic Solutions > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the rare July 17 1966 show – the only known performance of “In The Pines” – highlighted by a blistering Cream Puff War and powerful King Bee.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this early‑era recording, calling the SBD surprisingly crisp and even better than many later board tapes.  Musically the set is praised for its raw energy, rare songs (In The Pines, Cardboard Cowboy) and a standout Cream Puff War with Jerry’s snarling guitar tone.  The only drawback mentioned is the incomplete track list rather than any audio flaw.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (12 out of 15) are 4‑5 stars and specifically praise both the performance and the soundboard quality; only a few note missing songs, which affects completeness but not audio fidelity.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, full‑frequency SBD praised as better than many later boards; includes full ID‑4458 and ID‑13959 additions.  No major dropouts or muffling reported – the only complaint is missing tracks, not sound quality.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short early‑summer set that moves quickly through blues‑rock numbers, delivering high energy and rare material; the brief runtime is noted but doesn’t detract from the overall punch.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as having a "snarling" and "horny" guitar tone, especially on Cream Puff War.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass work isn’t singled out, but drumming (Bill Kreutzmann) is praised on Cold Rain & Snow, indicating a tight rhythm section.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted as absent on Cream Puff War; otherwise no specific comments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming on Cold Rain & Snow called "great" early in the band.
